neighbours.label: A person's own child or children as dependents someone looks after or brings along (with her child, no children to care for, for her two children), vs the same sentences with parents, pets or objects
fire: After the divorce she moved back to the village with her children.
The widow worked two jobs to feed her three children.
He had no children to look after, so he volunteered at the shelter.
The refugee arrived at the border carrying her child on her back.
Single mothers often struggle to find care for their children while working.
The old woman took in her grandson after his parents died.
She sold her jewelry to pay for her son's medicine.
The family lived in one room with their four children.
quiet: After the divorce she moved back to the village with her parents.
The widow worked two jobs to feed her three dogs.
He had no garden to look after, so he volunteered at the shelter.
The refugee arrived at the border carrying her bag on her back.
Single mothers often struggle to find time for themselves while working.
The old woman took in chickens after her husband died.
She sold her jewelry to pay for her own medicine.
The family lived in one room with their four cats.

predictions: child/children/son after a possessive in a care or dependence frame reach 0.3-0.6; the same frames with parents, dogs or bags stay under 0.1. Probes fired only on 'with her child', so this may fail.
